cards.title: Meta Releases Muse Glimmer: 30B Dense VLM with 2B Perception Encoder, Hybrid Attention, and Day-0 HF Support
cards.why_it_matters: A 30B open multimodal model from Meta with detailed architectural novelties — hybrid SWA/full-attention, NoPE, gated GQA, and a 2B ViT vision encoder — is a significant open-weight release you'll want to benchmark and understand architecturally.
cards.summary: Meta's Muse Glimmer is a 30B dense VLM comprising a 2B ViT-style Perception Encoder and a 28B text decoder. The decoder uses alternating sliding-window attention (2,048-token window, RoPE) and full-attention with NoPE in a (SWA, SWA, SWA, Full)×13 pattern, plus gated GQA with 16 query heads per KV head. An optional speculative decoding drafter on DFlash targets structured-content generation. Day-0 support ships in transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, and Inference Endpoints.

cards.title: NVIDIA Magpie TTS: 364M Open-Weights Multilingual TTS Adds Arabic, Korean, and Brazilian Portuguese
cards.why_it_matters: Open-weights, on-prem-deployable TTS with 12-language support and 32ms TTFA on B200 is directly relevant if you're building or evaluating voice pipeline infrastructure with latency and data-residency constraints.
cards.summary: NVIDIA Magpie Multilingual TTS is a 364M-parameter open-weights model supporting 12 languages, with the latest release adding Modern Standard Arabic, Korean, and Brazilian Portuguese. It reports 32ms time-to-first-audio on B200 hardware in on-prem deployment. The model supports code-switching for Hindi and Japanese via IPA grapheme-to-phoneme processing, and is deployable via NVIDIA NIM for full infrastructure control.

cards.title: Nathan Lambert's RLHF Textbook Ships: Full Post-Training Coverage from PPO to On-Policy Distillation
cards.why_it_matters: This is a rare practitioner-written, foundational resource on post-training — covering rejection sampling, outcome reward models, and modern RL algorithms — directly relevant to your daily research and engineering work.
cards.summary: Manning has published 'Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: Aligning and Post-training LLMs' by Nathan Lambert. The book covers RL intuitions (policy-gradient through PPO to GSPO and CISPO), rejection sampling, outcome reward models, and character training, with a last-minute section on on-policy distillation. Freely available online; 50% off until August 19 with code PBLambert. Includes a 12-hour YouTube course and code exercises.

cards.title: Hugging Face Proposes Offline Top-K Logit Caching + Chunked KL Loss to Slash Knowledge Distillation VRAM Cost
cards.why_it_matters: If you run distillation experiments, these two systems changes — caching teacher logits offline and chunking the KL loss — could make large-scale distillation feasible on far fewer GPUs, directly cutting your compute budget.
cards.summary: A Hugging Face paper introduces two changes for cheaper LLM knowledge distillation: (1) offline caching of the teacher's top-100 logits per token position, eliminating the need to keep the teacher in memory during training; (2) a fused chunked KL-divergence loss that avoids materializing the full vocabulary×sequence-length matrix. The paper reports that dense KL loss peaks at ~250GB VRAM (exceeding a single H200's 141GB), while the fused chunked loss peaks at ~128GB, enabling long-context distillation on a single GPU.

cards.title: Post-Grokking Generalization Collapse in Muon-Trained Transformers: A Representation-Readout Interface Failure
cards.why_it_matters: A mechanistically detailed study of optimizer-specific instability after grokking — identifying a failure mode unique to Muon's optimizer dynamics — is directly relevant to anyone using or studying Muon or studying grokking and generalization in transformers.
cards.summary: Across nine optimizer configurations on modular addition (mod 113), models trained with Muon on hidden matrices and AdamW on embeddings/output head grok faster but subsequently lose generalization. Post-grokking gradient falls to ~1e-6; Muon exhibits step-size elasticity of -0.03 versus +1.5 for AdamW, and the Muon group moves 8.0× faster per parameter. Freezing the embeddings/readout group prevents collapse across all five seeds over 451,400 post-grokking steps; freezing neither arm yields 137–321 sub-threshold evaluations. Fourier filtering separates circuit failure from masking, with the task-aligned family maintaining 100% accuracy in isolation.

cards.title: Safety Alignment in Diffusion LLMs Is Sparse and Transferable: Self-Pruning Raises ASR to 86.6% on Dream
cards.why_it_matters: Mechanistic safety vulnerabilities in diffusion LLMs — including cross-architecture transfer attacks and a black-box jailbreak framework achieving 74.3% ASR against Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite — are critical findings for anyone working on alignment, safety evals, or deploying DLLMs.
cards.summary: This paper shows safety alignment in diffusion LLMs (DLLMs) is sparse: DLLMs initialized from autoregressive models inherit the same safety neuron footprint, enabling transfer attacks. Self-pruning raises ASR from 2.6% to 73.8% on LLaDA and from 1.9% to 86.6% on Dream. Transfer pruning from Qwen2.5 raises ASR from 1.9% to 73.2% on Dream and from 7.0% to 86.3% on Fast-dLLM. The authors' SN-Guided Diffusion black-box jailbreak achieves transfer ASR of 77.1% on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, 86.9% on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and 74.3% on Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite using only 20 generation episodes per prompt.

cards.title: ML Fingerprinting for RIS-Aided mmWave Localization Under Cross-Link Interference at 28 GHz
cards.why_it_matters: A niche but technically concrete result on beam-domain ML localization under realistic interference — relevant if you work on 6G/wireless ML or want an example of applied ML regression under distributional shift from physical interference.
cards.summary: This paper proposes a beam-domain fingerprint framework mapping SNR across predefined RIS reflection states to UE azimuth angle and range without requiring CSI. Four ML regressors are evaluated at 28 GHz with a 20×20 RIS. Under clean conditions, KNN achieves 0.37° angle MAE and 4 cm range MAE; under cross-link interference these rise to 1.4° and 7.6 cm respectively. The paper finds interference degrades angle estimation substantially more than range estimation across all models.

cards.title: Wasserstein Policy Gradient Converges Exponentially for Entropy-Regularized Linear-Quadratic Control
cards.why_it_matters: A clean theoretical result showing WPG reduces to a finite-dimensional ODE with exponential global convergence for LQ control — with a convergence exponent that survives the zero-entropy limit — is a useful reference point for theoretically grounded RL algorithm analysis.
cards.summary: The paper studies Wasserstein policy gradient (WPG) for entropy-regularized discounted linear-quadratic control. A Bellman verification argument establishes that the optimal policy is linear-Gaussian, and the discounted-occupancy-weighted Wasserstein gradient is tangent to this class. WPG thus reduces to a finite-dimensional ODE for the feedback gain and action covariance. The ODE is proven globally well-posed with exponential convergence from any admissible initialization; the convergence exponent has a positive limit as entropy temperature tends to zero, with no exp(-c/τ) factor.
